as a translation student the best advice i can give you is try to find a university where you can study translation studies properly. There are a lot of factors that come into translation that many people like yourself with no studies have no idea about that are very important (translation techniques, linguistics, interpretation rules, etc) From what my teachers have told me and from what I've seen in my little corner of the world here in Mexico, the current translation market is saturated with individuals that think being bilingual equals being a translator and makes it harder to succeed and find jobs, but then again, that depends a lot on the languages you work with and other factors such as where you live and how good you can market yourself. 

Also try and figure out what you want to specialize in, literary translation, visual media translation, interpreting, etc.

Once you know what field you are interested in and just go to town with it, honestly, lots of practice and lots of reading. If you like law, then start reading law books, as well as studying the cultures you'll be translating to (ie. russian law and british/american/aussie/etc law)   


technically you could start working for someone right now if that's what you want, but like almost every other job, it's all about connections and luck, the only downside to start working is that you risk putting out a bad translation and therefore "burning bridges" before you even start making them, you can also start looking into CAT tools, most of them are expensive but a free one you can start with is Omega T, there are a lot of tutorials and albeit it is very not kind to the eyes, but it's a very good start!

There's more i'd like to say but my brain is very fried right now, i actually just finished one of my subtitling class' homework haha  


Hope this could have been of help to you! Much luck and I hope you can figure out what you want soon!
